아내.forms: 아내가 · 아내를 · honorific: 부인 (someone else's wife)
아내.x: I go to the market with my wife.
아내.e: Use 아내 for your own wife.
아내.t: For someone else's wife, use 부인 or 사모님. In casual speech many people also say 와이프.

콜라.x: I ordered a hamburger and a cola.
콜라.e: From English 'cola'. Ask for 콜라 rather than 'Coke'.

데려가다.m: to take (a person or animal) along
데려가다.x: I'm going to take the kids to the zoo this weekend.
데려가다.e: 데리다 (to have someone with you) + 가다 (to go): take someone along.
데려가다.t: Use 데려가다 for people and animals, 가져가다 for things; for elders say 모시고 가다.

과제.x: I'm busy because I have to turn in an assignment by tomorrow.
과제.t: University students say 과제; 숙제 sounds more like grade-school homework.

고소하다.m: nutty, savory (like sesame or roasted grains)
고소하다.x: I added sesame oil, and now it smells really nutty.
고소하다.e: Homonym warning: a different 고소하다 means 'to sue'.
고소하다.t: Used for the smell of roasted sesame, nuts or fresh bread — English has no exact match.

내년.x: I'm going to graduate from college next year.

모기.ex: 어젯밤에 모기 때문에 잠을 못 잤어요.
모기.x: I couldn't sleep last night because of mosquitoes.
모기.t: Mosquitoes 'bite' with 물다: 모기한테 물렸어요 'I got bitten by a mosquito.'

냄새가 나다.forms: 냄새가 나요 · 냄새가 났어요; N에서 냄새가 나다
냄새가 나다.m: to smell, to give off a smell
냄새가 나다.ex: 엄마가 요리하셔서 부엌에서 맛있는 냄새가 나요.
냄새가 나다.x: Mom is cooking, so something smells delicious in the kitchen.
냄새가 나다.t: Mark the source with 에서: 방에서 이상한 냄새가 나요 'The room smells weird.'

드럼.x: My younger sibling plays drums in the school band.
드럼.t: Play drums: 드럼을 치다, the same verb as for piano and guitar. Traditional Korean drums are 북 and 장구.

피로.ex: 요즘 일이 많아서 피로가 많이 쌓였어요.
피로.x: I've had a lot of work lately, so fatigue has really built up.

소음.ex: 밤마다 위층 소음 때문에 잠을 못 자요.
소음.x: I can't sleep every night because of the noise upstairs.
소음.t: 층간 소음, noise between apartment floors, is a very common neighbor complaint in Korea.

시민.x: Many citizens gathered in the square on the weekend.
시민.t: 시민 is a city's residents or citizens in a civic sense; 국민 is the people of a whole nation.

주제.x: The topic of this presentation is environmental problems.
주제.t: 주제 is what something is about; 제목 is the title written at the top.

대통령.x: In Korea, citizens directly elect the president every five years.
대통령.t: Pronounced [대통녕]: ㄹ after ㅇ becomes ㄴ. For a company president, use 사장 or 회장.

담임.m: homeroom teacher; being in charge of a class
담임.x: This year's homeroom teacher is very kind.
담임.e: Literally 'carrying the duty' — the teacher responsible for a class.

이전.x: The house I used to live in was far from school.
이전.t: Don't confuse it with a different 이전 meaning 'relocation', as in 사무실 이전 'office move.'

기초.ex: 외국어는 처음에 기초를 잘 배워야 해요.
기초.x: With a foreign language, you have to learn the basics well at the start.
기초.e: Literally 'base stone' — the stone a pillar stands on.
기초.t: 기초 suggests a starting level (기초 한국어 'beginner Korean'); 기본 means the standard essentials.

관리하다.m: to manage, to take care of, to maintain
관리하다.x: I exercise every day to take good care of my health.
관리하다.t: Pronounced [괄리하다]: ㄴ next to ㄹ becomes ㄹ.

느끼하다.m: greasy, oily, too rich; cheesy, sleazy (person)
느끼하다.ex: 피자를 많이 먹었더니 속이 좀 느끼해요.
느끼하다.x: I ate a lot of pizza, and now my stomach feels a bit greasy.
느끼하다.t: Also slang for a cheesy, sleazy person or line: 느끼한 말.

참고.ex: 이 자료가 숙제에 참고가 될 거예요.
참고.x: This material will be a useful reference for your homework.
참고.t: 참고로 means 'for your information' or 'FYI' at the start of a sentence.

세균.x: There are lots of germs on your hands, so wash them often.

언론.x: The incident was widely reported in the press.
언론.t: Pronounced [얼론]: ㄴ before ㄹ becomes ㄹ (liquidization).

산불.x: Wildfires often break out in the dry spring.
산불.e: Literally 'mountain fire'; 불 is the native Korean word for fire.
산불.t: Fires 'come out' in Korean: 산불이 나다 = a wildfire breaks out.

판단.x: That situation called for a quick judgment.
판단.e: Literally 'judge and cut': making a clean call.

노선.ex: 이 버스 노선은 시청 앞까지 가요.
노선.x: This bus route goes to the front of City Hall.

노선.ex: 두 정당은 경제 정책 노선이 다릅니다.
노선.x: The two parties follow different lines on economic policy.
노선.t: Context decides the meaning: 버스 노선 is a bus route, 정치 노선 a political line.

스킨케어.x: I always do my skincare before bed.
스킨케어.t: Watch out: 스킨 alone usually means toner in Korea, as in the basic routine 스킨 → 로션.

리듬.ex: 아이들이 음악 리듬에 맞춰 춤을 추고 있어요.
리듬.x: The children are dancing to the rhythm of the music.
리듬.e: From English 'rhythm'; Korean adds a vowel: 리-듬.
리듬.t: Common pattern: 리듬에 맞춰 'in time with the rhythm'; also 생활 리듬 'daily rhythm'.

무죄.ex: 그는 오랜 재판 끝에 무죄 판결을 받았어요.
무죄.x: After a long trial, he was found not guilty.
무죄.e: Literally 'no crime'; 무- = without: 무료, 무죄.

그리하여.m: thus, and so, as a result
그리하여.ex: 그는 꾸준히 노력했습니다. 그리하여 마침내 꿈을 이루었습니다.
그리하여.x: He worked steadily. And so, he finally achieved his dream.
그리하여.e: From 그리하다 'to do so' — 'having done so'.
그리하여.t: Written or storytelling style; in conversation, use 그래서.

배제하다.m: to exclude, to rule out, to leave out
배제하다.ex: 사고 가능성을 완전히 배제할 수는 없어요.
배제하다.x: We can't completely rule out the possibility of an accident.
배제하다.t: Common phrase: 가능성을 배제할 수 없다 'cannot rule out the possibility'.

깔다.forms: 깔아요 · 깔았어요 · 깔 거예요 · 까세요 (ㄹ drops)
깔다.m: to spread (out), to lay down; to install (an app)
깔다.x: We spread out a mat on the ground in the park and sat down.
깔다.e: Its passive 깔리다 means 'to be spread' or 'to be pinned under'.
깔다.t: Casual: 앱을 깔다 means to install an app.

흘러가다.m: to flow (along); to pass (time); to go, turn out (a situation)
흘러가다.x: My four years of college went by really fast.

기발하다.x: My friend came up with a really clever idea.
기발하다.e: Literally 'strangely outstanding' — standing out by being unusual.

부문.ex: 그 영화는 작품상 부문에서 상을 받았어요.
부문.x: That film won in the Best Picture category.
부문.e: Literally 'section gate': one branch of a larger field.
부문.t: Don't confuse 부문 (sector, category) with 부분 (part, portion).

초점.ex: 이번 회의는 비용 절감에 초점을 맞췄어요.
초점.x: This meeting focused on cutting costs.
초점.e: Literally 'scorching point': where a lens gathers sunlight and burns.

멀미.x: I get carsick if I'm on a bus for a long time.
멀미.t: Use 멀미가 나다 or 멀미하다. 차멀미 = carsickness, 뱃멀미 = seasickness, 멀미약 = motion-sickness medicine.

퇴임.x: After leaving office, the president returned to his hometown.
퇴임.t: Opposite: 취임 (taking office); 퇴임 is a normal end of service, unlike 사임 (resigning).

분열.ex: 당 내부의 분열이 점점 심해지고 있어요.
분열.x: The division within the party is getting worse.
분열.t: Pronounced [부녈] — the ㄴ batchim links into 열.

재심.m: retrial, review of a final judgment
재심.ex: 새로운 증거가 나와서 법원이 재심을 결정했어요.
재심.x: New evidence came out, so the court decided on a retrial.

전이.ex: 다행히 암이 다른 장기로 전이되지 않았어요.
전이.x: Fortunately, the cancer hasn't spread to other organs.

진술하다.m: to state, to testify, to give a statement
진술하다.ex: 목격자는 경찰에게 사고 상황을 자세히 진술했습니다.
진술하다.x: The witness gave the police a detailed statement about the accident.
진술하다.e: Literally 'lay out and state' — telling the facts formally.
진술하다.t: Used in legal and police contexts: 진술을 번복하다 'to recant one's statement.'

재편되다.m: to be reorganized, to be restructured, to be realigned
재편되다.x: The market structure was reorganized around large corporations.
재편되다.t: Common in news: 정계 재편 = political realignment.

참담하다.ex: 시험 결과가 참담해서 할 말이 없었어요.
참담하다.x: The test results were so dismal that I was speechless.
참담하다.t: Often for feelings or outcomes: 참담한 심정, 참담한 결과.

그럼에도.ex: 그럼에도 불구하고 그는 끝까지 포기하지 않았어요.
그럼에도.x: Nevertheless, he didn't give up until the end.
그럼에도.e: A contraction of 그러함에도 'even though it is so'.

양적 완화.ex: 중앙은행은 경기를 살리기 위해 양적 완화를 실시했습니다.
양적 완화.x: The central bank carried out quantitative easing to revive the economy.
양적 완화.t: Its opposite in the news is 긴축 (tightening), as in 양적 긴축.

훈계하다.ex: 아버지는 거짓말을 한 아들을 조용히 훈계하셨어요.
훈계하다.x: The father quietly admonished his son for lying.

처지.ex: 저도 같은 처지라서 그 마음을 잘 알아요.
처지.x: I'm in the same situation, so I know exactly how you feel.

둘러대다.m: to make up an excuse, explain away, cover up with an excuse
둘러대다.ex: 늦은 이유를 묻자 그는 차가 막혔다고 둘러댔어요.
둘러대다.x: When asked why he was late, he made the excuse that traffic was bad.
둘러대다.e: From 두르다 'to wrap around' + 대다: talking your way around the truth.

지정학.x: He is researching geopolitics at a university.

수녀.ex: 그 수녀는 평생 가난한 아이들을 돌보며 살았어요.
수녀.x: That nun spent her whole life caring for poor children.
수녀.e: Literally 'cultivating woman'; 녀 becomes 여 at the start of a word, as in 여자.
수녀.t: Address a nun as 수녀님, with the honorific -님.

애수.x: You can feel the melancholy of autumn in that song.
애수.e: Literally 'grief and sorrow' — a gentle, lingering sadness.

기혈.m: qi and blood, vital energy and blood
기혈.ex: 한의학에서는 기혈 순환이 건강의 핵심이라고 봐요.
기혈.x: Korean medicine sees the circulation of qi and blood as the key to health.
기혈.e: Literally 'energy and blood' — the two flows of traditional medicine.

변인.x: In this experiment, temperature is an important variable.
변인.t: 변인 is common in science education; statistics and math usually say 변수 instead.

주기율표.x: We had to memorize the periodic table in chemistry class.

초판.x: The first edition of this book was published in 1950.
초판.t: 초판 1쇄 means 'first edition, first printing', the copy collectors want most.

절판.ex: 그 책은 이미 절판되어서 구하기가 어려워요.
절판.x: That book is already out of print, so it's hard to find.
절판.t: Usually used as the verb 절판되다 'to go out of print.'

필체.ex: 편지의 필체를 보고 누가 썼는지 바로 알았어요.
필체.x: I knew right away who wrote the letter from the handwriting.
필체.e: Literally 'brush style': the way a person's hand shapes letters.

단조.ex: 이 노래는 단조라서 그런지 조금 슬프게 들려요.
단조.x: Maybe because it's in a minor key, this song sounds a bit sad.
단조.e: Homonym alert: 단조롭다 'monotonous' comes from a different 단조.

문신.ex: 고려 시대에는 문신이 무신보다 더 좋은 대우를 받았어요.
문신.x: In the Goryeo period, civil officials were treated better than military officials.
문신.e: Literally 'subject of letters', an official who serves with the pen.
문신.t: Homonym alert: 문신 also means a tattoo, written with different characters.

근절하다.ex: 정부는 학교 폭력을 근절하기 위해 노력하고 있습니다.
근절하다.x: The government is working to root out school violence.

하위문화.x: Hip-hop started as a subculture and became mainstream.

녹색성장.ex: 정부는 녹색성장을 국가 발전 전략으로 내세웠습니다.
녹색성장.x: The government put forward green growth as its national development strategy.
녹색성장.e: Literally 'green-colored growth': growth that is eco-friendly.

산출하다.ex: 보험료는 나이와 건강 상태를 기준으로 산출합니다.
산출하다.x: Insurance premiums are calculated based on age and health.
산출하다.t: Homonym: 산출하다 (産出) means 'to produce (goods or resources).'

섬멸하다.x: Our forces annihilated the enemy's main unit.
섬멸하다.e: Literally 'annihilate and destroy': leaving nothing behind.

체념하다.m: to give up hope, to resign oneself (to)
체념하다.ex: 그는 합격을 체념하고 다른 길을 찾았어요.
체념하다.x: He gave up hope of passing and looked for another path.
체념하다.e: Originally Buddhist 'seeing the truth'; now accepting that something can't be changed.
체념하다.t: 체념하다 stresses quiet acceptance; 포기하다 simply means stopping an effort.

가치판단.x: Scientists try to avoid value judgments in their research.

견마지로.x: Though I lack much, I will devote my humble efforts to the country.
견마지로.e: Literally 'the labor of a dog or horse': a modest way to pledge loyalty.
견마지로.t: A humble expression used about one's own efforts, never about someone else's.

적수공권.ex: 그는 적수공권으로 서울에 올라와 회사를 세웠어요.
적수공권.x: He came to Seoul with nothing and built a company.
적수공권.t: Commonly appears as 적수공권으로 'with nothing to one's name.'
